channel.title: Lumeshot
channel.description: Updates for Lumeshot, a screenshot and screen-recording tool for macOS.

item.description:
No changes to the app. This release is identical to v0.1.15 and exists so the automatic updater has something to update *to*.
v0.1.15 introduced Sparkle, but a copy of it finds only its own entry in the feed, so nothing about the download-and-install path could be exercised until a newer release existed. This is that release.
If you are reading this inside Lumeshot's update window, the part that needed testing has already worked: the app checked the feed, found this version, and fetched these notes. Installing it exercises the rest — verifying the signature, replacing the app in place, and relaunching.
If you are on v0.1.15 there is nothing to gain by updating, beyond confirming that updating works.

Lumeshot now updates itself, and a code review of the whole app turned up twelve defects — several of which could lose a capture, an upload, or a credential.
Eleven of them are listed below. The twelfth stopped the app launching at all and never reached a published build, so no released version was affected by it.
## Automatic updates
Lumeshot checks for updates daily and on demand, then downloads, verifies and installs them in place. Downloading a dmg and dragging it to Applications is no longer part of updating.
This release is the one you install by hand; from here on it updates itself.
## Fixes that protect your data
- **Uploads no longer overwrite each other.** With **Save a copy** switched off, every capture was uploaded under the same name, so destinations addressed by filename — S3, SFTP and FTP — replaced the previous capture each time, and with no local copy there was nothing to recover. Each upload now gets its own name. - **A failed uploader edit no longer destroys working credentials.** If saving an edited uploader failed part way, it could leave the destination with no credentials at all, or with a rejected new key sitting beside the restored old password — and SFTP would then use the rejected key. - **Editing an SFTP uploader keeps its pinned host key.** Renaming a destination could silently discard the fingerprint learned on the first connection, after which Lumeshot trusted whatever the server presented next. A pin is now kept unless you point the destination at a different host or port. - **Re-uploading a capture cannot delete the earlier upload.** A failed second upload inherited the first one's remote deletion link, so deleting the failure deleted the copy that had worked.
## Fixes that protect what you meant to hide
- **A crop that cannot be applied stops the export.** Drawing a crop outside the image — easy to do in the grey margins around it — used to export the whole, uncropped screenshot instead. Crops are now confined to the image, and an export that still cannot apply one shows an error rather than sending the original. - **A redaction that fails to render stops the export.** If blur or pixelate could not be drawn, the image was delivered without them. Copy, Save and Upload now refuse, and the editor stays open so nothing is lost. - **Upload failures no longer log the server's reply.** A server that echoes your request back in an error could write an API key or a deletion token into `~/Library/Logs/Lumeshot.log`. The reason for the failure is still recorded.
## Other fixes
- **A failed upload is reported as a failure.** A custom uploader whose response was missing the value its URL template asked for could report success and copy a broken link to the clipboard. - **FTP directories starting with `/` are absolute.** They were being treated as relative to the login directory, so uploads landed somewhere other than the configured path while the copied link claimed otherwise. If you worked around this by writing the path relative to your login directory, drop the leading slash to keep the old behaviour. Servers that lock the login to `/` are unaffected. - **The menu bar no longer claims to be recording after a failed start.** It could show a running timer with no recording behind it, which stopping would not clear. - **Settings changes no longer overwrite each other.** A background change, such as learning an SSH host key mid-upload, could discard a preference saved at the same moment.
## Upgrading
Download the dmg and replace your existing copy. Your settings, history and stored credentials are kept.
